doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Kenny Dorham and trumpeter Idrees Sulieman
summary: He had a band with Dorham, and says Sulieman was the best trumpeter but left because of prejudice against Muslim names.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So you had Horace Silver and Blue Mitchell on the date. Had you been working with Arthur Taylor?
Well, that’s a helluva band to be working with. Were they with you at Minton’s?
Actually, we had a band with Kenny Dorham, but Kenny got busted or something. He couldn’t make the date. We had a band with Kenny Dorham and Art Taylor and Gene Ramey.
You were pretty close to Kenny Dorham.
Yeah. We had a band together.
I guess you recorded a sextet thing in 1954. How did the relationship start?
Well, it was just a matter that I had to do a record date, and I needed some musicians I thought could make it.
Had you been playing with him before that?
Yeah, I’d been playing with him a little.
What kind of guy was he?
Nice guy. Very nice guy. Very intelligent. But he had a lip problem, you know.

Chops problem. But all of them did, Miles and all of them. Chops problem. I don’t know what it was. Probably they didn’t learn how to play correct. The best trumpet player around New York during those times was a guy named Idees Sulieman. He could play better than any of those guys. But he knew he wasn’t going to get no gigs because all the promoters and all the club owners were Jewish, so he just packed up and went overseas.
They didn’t want a guy with a Muslim name, an Islamic name.
No. Muslim was out. Back then, the Muslims was out.
I guess Sahib Shihab had that problem, too.
